fertilizer_timing: Basal (all P and K + part of N) applied before final harrowing. Wet season (2-split): remaining N applied 5-7 days before panicle initiation. Dry season (3-split): 1/3 of N at 5-7 days before panicle initiation, 1/6 of N at 10% flowering.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer incorporated into the soil before final harrowing. Topdress fertilizer is broadcast after the field is saturated (or has a 2-3 cm water depth) and weeds are removed, to maximize uptake.
watering_guide: Saturate the field before each topdress application; maintain a shallow water depth (2-3 cm) if full irrigation isn't available.
guidance_source_title: DA-ATI CAR - Simple Fertilizer Computations Using Split Method of Application in Rice Production (citing PhilRice Rice Production Technoguide)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Saturate the field... maintain a shallow water depth (2-3 cm)"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Keep saturated to shallow-flooded through most stages; AWD practitioners can let it drop to ~70% before re-flooding.

fertilizer_timing: All P and K plus half of N applied as basal at planting. Remaining half of N side-dressed 20-24 days after emergence, right before hilling-up.
fertilizer_method: Basal: complete fertilizer (14-14-14) placed in furrows and covered with ~2 cm of soil. Side-dress: ammonium sulfate or urea placed 4-5 cm from the plant base, then covered by hilling-up soil.
watering_guide: Ensure adequate soil moisture at planting; irrigate during dry-season planting, especially in the window from knee-high through tasseling/silking, when moisture stress hurts yield most.
guidance_source_title: Corn Production Guide: Nutrient Management (Philippine agricultural extension guide reflecting BPI/DA practice)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "...especially in the window from knee-high through tasseling/silking, when moisture stress hurts yield most"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Widen the trigger to ~50-55% during general vegetative growth, but hold the higher end through tasseling/silking.

fertilizer_timing: Areas with irregular rainfall, distinct dry season, or sandy soil: split twice a year (half at the start of the rainy season, half six months before the rainy season ends). Areas with uniform rainfall: split during the 1st year, then apply once annually thereafter.
fertilizer_method: Flat areas: broadcast in the ring-weeded area (1.0-1.5 m radius around the base) and fork-in to incorporate. Hilly areas: place in 8-10 equidistant holes, 5 cm deep, around the base, then cover with soil.
watering_guide: Water young palms/seedlings regularly during dry months; mature palms are largely rainfall-dependent but benefit from supplemental watering during prolonged drought.
guidance_source_title: Philippine Coconut Authority (Davao Research Center) - Techno Guide on Fertilization No. 01/2019: Fertilization Guide for Coconuts
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water young palms/seedlings regularly... mature palms are largely rainfall-dependent"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Only irrigate mature palms if the reading stays low through a prolonged dry spell.

fertilizer_timing: First year: apply every 4 months. Double the rate for succeeding years (Saba banana recommendation; other varieties follow a similar split-every-few-months pattern).
fertilizer_method: Mix complete fertilizer (14-14-14), urea (45-0-0), and muriate of potash (0-0-60); apply at roughly 440 g per hill, worked into the soil around the base.
watering_guide: Plant at the start of the rainy season for adequate establishment moisture; keep soil consistently moist but well-drained - banana has a shallow root system sensitive to both drought and waterlogging.
guidance_source_title: DA Bureau of Plant Industry / DA-Cagayan de Oro - Saba Banana Production Guide
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "keep soil consistently moist but well-drained - banana has a shallow root system sensitive to both drought and waterlogging"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Avoid letting it fall much below 60% (drought) or sit saturated for long (root rot risk).

fertilizer_timing: Basal at planting; side-dress remaining N and K in splits during the tillering stage (30-45 days) and again at the grand growth stage (60-90 days).
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer placed in the furrow before covering with soil; side-dress fertilizer placed along the row, followed by hilling-up.
watering_guide: Irrigate during dry months, especially at tillering and grand growth stages; reduce watering as the crop approaches maturity to favor sugar accumulation over vegetative growth.
guidance_source_title: DOST-PCAARRD Sugarcane Industry Strategic S&T Plan (industry context; specific split-timing reflects standard Philippine sugarcane agronomic practice, not a single primary document)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "...especially at tillering and grand growth stages; reduce watering as the crop approaches maturity"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: The taper before harvest is intentional - drier soil favors sugar accumulation over vegetative growth.

fertilizer_timing: Applied in split doses roughly every 2-3 months from planting until flower induction, based on soil/leaf analysis where available.
fertilizer_method: Granular fertilizer applied into the leaf axils (the funnel-shaped leaf base) for slow release, or as a foliar spray for faster uptake during active growth.
watering_guide: Water consistently during establishment; pineapple tolerates drought once established but yields best with steady moisture through vegetative growth.
guidance_source_title: DOST-PCAARRD Queen Pineapple program (fertilization based on soil analysis) and general pineapple fertigation practice
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water consistently during establishment; pineapple tolerates drought once established"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Don't chase a high reading once established - pineapple stores water in its leaves.

fertilizer_timing: Regular NPK fertilization at the start of the rainy season and after harvest/pruning. For flower induction (used to produce off-season fruit): trees must have mature leaves (7-8 months old); potassium nitrate is sprayed once leaves reach that maturity, with a possible second spray 10-14 days later if flowering is poor.
fertilizer_method: Soil-applied NPK broadcast under the canopy drip-line. Potassium nitrate (KNO3) for flower induction is a foliar spray, thoroughly wetting the leaves - soil-applied fertilizer cannot reach developing flowers directly.
watering_guide: Water young trees regularly; for induced flowering, avoid rain/irrigation for at least 6 hours after spraying, and water regularly again once fruit set begins.
guidance_source_title: Philippine Fruit Trees Production Guide; Manila Bulletin flower-induction reporting (note: potassium nitrate purchase/possession in the Philippines is regulated by the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office under RA 9516 due to its dual use in explosives)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water young trees regularly... water regularly again once fruit set begins"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: For induced flowering: no irrigation for 6 hours after the KNO3 spray, then resume toward the higher end once fruit set starts.

fertilizer_timing: Fertilize based on soil test results, typically in 2-3 split applications aligned with the rainy season.
fertilizer_method: Apply in a ring around the base at the drip-line; incorporate lightly with soil or mulch.
watering_guide: Water young plants regularly during dry months; shaded, established plants need less frequent supplemental watering.
guidance_source_title: Coffee Farming and Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide; general practice, not a single primary-agency fertilizer schedule)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water young plants regularly... shaded, established plants need less frequent supplemental watering"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Shade reduces evaporation, so mature shaded coffee can sit lower without stress.

fertilizer_timing: Age-based schedule from field planting (per PCARRD 1989 recommendation): fertilizer amounts increase as trees mature, applied at set month intervals after field planting rather than a single flat rate.
fertilizer_method: Applied per plant in a ring around the base at the drip-line; basal fertilizer at planting is important to establish young trees.
watering_guide: Water young trees regularly, especially during establishment; mature trees under shade need water mainly during prolonged dry spells.
guidance_source_title: DA-HVCDP Cacao Production Guide (fertilizer rates per PCARRD, 1989)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water young trees regularly, especially during establishment; mature trees under shade need water mainly during prolonged dry spells"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Prioritize the young/establishment stage - that's where moisture matters most.

fertilizer_timing: Recommended practice is 3 applications per year (traditional smallholder practice often applies none, which the industry roadmap identifies as a key yield gap).
fertilizer_method: Broadcast around the base of each hill and incorporate lightly into the soil.
watering_guide: Needs consistent soil moisture, especially in the first year; grows best in areas with well-distributed rainfall.
guidance_source_title: Philippine Abaca Industry Roadmap 2018-2022 (DA / PhilFIDA)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Needs consistent soil moisture, especially in the first year"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Treat a reading below 60% as a warning sign, particularly in year one.

fertilizer_timing: National Fertilizer Recommendation (NFR): 8 bags of 14-14-14 per hectare. One-third of N and K plus all P applied as basal; remainder applied at 2.5 and 5 months after planting.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer applied in the planting furrow; remaining splits placed around the base of the plant and covered lightly with soil.
watering_guide: Water regularly during the first 2-3 months for establishment; cassava is drought-tolerant afterward and needs minimal irrigation.
guidance_source_title: PhilRootcrops / DA - Towards Increasing Cassava Production in the Philippines through Site-Specific Nutrient Management
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water regularly during the first 2-3 months for establishment; cassava is drought-tolerant afterward and needs minimal irrigation"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: After establishment you can let the reading run low - cassava is highly drought-tolerant.

fertilizer_timing: Apply at planting time; amount depends on soil fertility (poor soil: 4-6 bags complete fertilizer/ha; moderately fertile: 4 bags/ha; already-fertile soil: additional fertilizer usually not advised).
fertilizer_method: Applied 8-10 cm from the base of the plant, or broadcast in the furrows and covered with soil. Compost/organic fertilizer at ~3 tons/ha is also recommended.
watering_guide: Plant vine cuttings on ridges during the rainy season (to avoid waterlogging) or in furrows during the dry season (to use residual soil moisture); avoid overwatering near harvest.
guidance_source_title: Sweet Potato Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide reflecting DA/BPI practice)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "...to avoid waterlogging... avoid overwatering near harvest"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Deliberately reduce watering as harvest nears to prevent cracking/rot in the tubers.

fertilizer_timing: Nitrogen minimal (legume, fixes its own); phosphorus important especially on sandy soil; potassium and calcium (lime/dolomite) applied to support grain fill, informed by soil test.
fertilizer_method: Potassium should be placed deep enough to reach the root/pegging zone; calcium source (lime/dolomite) applied per agriculturist's recommendation to ensure well-filled pods.
watering_guide: October planting: little irrigation needed until December. February planting: water 3-4 times. Water again once pods/grains begin to form; wet the soil to about 30 cm deep when irrigating.
guidance_source_title: Peanut Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide reflecting DA/BPI practice)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "October planting: little irrigation needed until December... Water again once pods/grains begin to form"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Raise toward the higher end specifically once pods/grains begin forming.

fertilizer_timing: Light basal fertilizer at planting; foliar fertilizer high in potassium and phosphorus sprayed at 25-30 days after planting (DAP) and again after the 1st and 2nd pod-priming, to support 3 priming cycles.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer broadcast or banded at planting; foliar fertilizer sprayed directly on the plants (can be combined with compatible insecticides).
watering_guide: Needs sufficient water during germination, vegetative growth, and flowering; fairly drought-tolerant otherwise, and often grown on residual soil moisture after rice.
guidance_source_title: DA-HVCDP Mungbean Production Guide
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Needs sufficient water during germination, vegetative growth, and flowering; fairly drought-tolerant otherwise"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Often grown on residual soil moisture after rice - treat this as a target to supplement toward, not a strict daily floor.

fertilizer_timing: Basal at transplanting; side-dress fertilizer applied per a set schedule through the fruiting period.
fertilizer_method: Conventional method: fertilizer applied directly to furrows/ridges via side-dressing or shallow furrows. Plastic-mulch method: fertilizer applied beside planting rows, with basal and side-dress split via drenching solutions on a set schedule.
watering_guide: Water requirement is about 35-40 mm/week; moderately sensitive to flooding, and especially moisture-sensitive during flowering and fruit enlargement.
guidance_source_title: Eggplant Production Guide for the Philippines (UPLB Institute of Plant Breeding / DA-BAR)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "moderately sensitive to flooding, and especially moisture-sensitive during flowering and fruit enlargement"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Avoid pushing much above 70-75% given the flooding sensitivity.

fertilizer_timing: Basal (14-14-14) applied 3-5 days after transplanting; side-dress (urea + muriate of potash, 2:1 ratio) applied about two weeks later, placed 6-8 cm from the base.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer applied per hill and mixed into soil; side-dress fertilizer banded near (not touching) the plant base to avoid root burn.
watering_guide: 4-5 irrigations from transplanting to about 14 days before the last harvest; irrigate just enough to moisten the root zone, since tomato is sensitive to flooding - irrigation is done weekly during fruiting and reduced to every 10 days near the last harvest.
guidance_source_title: Tomato Production Guide (UPLB Institute of Plant Breeding; DA-RFU 4A / Bureau of Agricultural Research technology package)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "irrigate just enough to moisten the root zone, since tomato is sensitive to flooding... reduced to every 10 days near the last harvest"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Treat any reading above ~75-80% as a drainage problem, not a target.

fertilizer_timing: Basal complete fertilizer (14-14-14) at planting; side-dress with urea (46-0-0) at 30 days after emergence.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer applied per hill at planting; side-dress fertilizer applied near the plant base and covered with soil.
watering_guide: Water regularly, especially during flowering and fruiting; okra responds well to consistent moisture but tolerates brief dry spells better than flooding.
guidance_source_title: DA-ATI Region 7 - Okra Production Guide
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "responds well to consistent moisture but tolerates brief dry spells better than flooding"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: When in doubt, err toward the lower end given the flood sensitivity.

fertilizer_timing: Basal complete fertilizer (14-14-14) at about 25 g/hill at planting. Side-dress with urea and muriate of potash: 10-20 g/hill once a month in dry season, or 5-10 g/hill more frequently in wet season.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer applied per hill at planting; side-dress fertilizer buried near the base and covered with at least 6 cm of soil.
watering_guide: Water every other 1-2 days and whenever fertilizer is applied; sensitive to waterlogging, so ensure good drainage despite frequent watering.
guidance_source_title: DA-ATI CAR - Ampalaya (Bitter Gourd) Production Guide
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water every other 1-2 days... sensitive to waterlogging, so ensure good drainage despite frequent watering"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Needs frequent light irrigation to hold this range, paired with good drainage.

fertilizer_timing: Young trees: 50-100 g ammonium sulfate/urea per tree monthly for the first year, every 4 months thereafter, increasing to 200-300 g/tree in year two. Bearing trees (year 4+): switch to complete fertilizer (ammophos + potash) to boost fruiting; mature trees (8-10 years): 2-3 kg fertilizer, 3 times a year (before rains, after flowering, after harvest).
fertilizer_method: Applied around the base of the tree; organic compost applied twice a year in addition to inorganic fertilizer.
watering_guide: Young trees (first two years) need regular watering to establish strong roots; mature trees need less frequent watering and should never be left in standing water.
guidance_source_title: Calamansi Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Young trees... need regular watering... mature trees need less frequent watering and should never be left in standing water"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Never let mature trees' reading indicate standing water - that's an explicit warning in the guide.

fertilizer_timing: Start with a handful (5-10 g) of complete fertilizer (14-14-14) at planting. Apply 60 g ammonium sulfate once the plant is established, repeated every 6 weeks until 1 year old. Thereafter, 225 g ammonium sulfate every 3 months, plus 450 g superphosphate at the start of the rainy season each year.
fertilizer_method: Mixed into the soil at the bottom of the planting hole initially; later applications placed around the base of the plant, avoiding direct trunk contact.
watering_guide: Water consistently - papaya is sensitive to both drought and waterlogging, so moderate, steady moisture matters more than heavy occasional watering.
guidance_source_title: Papaya Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "sensitive to both drought and waterlogging, so moderate, steady moisture matters more than heavy occasional watering"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Hold this range steadily rather than swinging high-low.

fertilizer_timing: Fertilizer type/amount should follow local soil analysis; in the absence of one, provincial recommendations (e.g., Ilocos Norte) provide a fallback rate.
fertilizer_method: Commonly grown under mulch (typically rice straw); organic fertilizer is considered especially effective for garlic in the Philippines.
watering_guide: Irrigation frequency depends on soil type: clay loam is typically irrigated about 3 times during the cropping period, sandy soil more frequently. Water should never stand in the field for more than 6 hours.
guidance_source_title: DA Regional Field Office 02 - Garlic Production Guide
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "clay loam is typically irrigated about 3 times... sandy soil more frequently. Water should never stand in the field for more than 6 hours"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Sandy soil needs more frequent irrigation to hold this same range than clay loam does.

fertilizer_timing: Basal: all phosphate (0-18-0) plus half of the ammonium sulfate (21-0-0) and muriate of potash (0-0-60). Side-dress the remaining half at 30, 45, and 60 days after transplanting.
fertilizer_method: Basal fertilizer incorporated before transplanting; side-dress fertilizer applied along rows at each interval. High nitrogen rates late in the cycle should be avoided - they shorten bulb storage life.
watering_guide: Irrigate every 4-7 days depending on soil type; stop irrigation 2-3 weeks before harvest, or once 20-30% of the tops fold over - the last irrigation before that point should be light.
guidance_source_title: Onion Production Guide (Philippine agricultural extension guide reflecting DA-RFU 02 practice)
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Irrigate every 4-7 days... stop irrigation 2-3 weeks before harvest, or once 20-30% of the tops fold over"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: The pre-harvest taper is intentional - it improves bulb storage life.

fertilizer_timing: Basal at transplanting, with NTA-recommended soil conditioner applied per the official Virginia/Burley technoguide; timing coordinated with topping before full bloom.
fertilizer_method: Follow National Tobacco Administration (NTA)-recommended crop protection and soil conditioning practices; topping (removing the flower head) redirects growth into leaf size and quality.
watering_guide: Water consistently during establishment and vegetative growth; reduce as leaves approach maturity to support proper curing quality.
guidance_source_title: National Tobacco Administration - Tobacco Production Manual, Flue-Cured (Virginia) Technoguide 2020-2021
pct_basis_phrase_from_watering_guide: "Water consistently during establishment and vegetative growth; reduce as leaves approach maturity"
soil_moisture_sensor_note: Lowering the reading before harvest supports proper leaf curing quality.

fertilizer_timing: Immature trees: phosphate (often rock phosphate) applied during establishment years. Mature trees (after tapping begins): phosphate and calcium-containing fertilizers applied sparingly, since calcium can reduce latex yield by promoting vessel plugging.
fertilizer_method: Applied around the base per standard smallholder practice; liming avoided unless soil is excessively acidic.
watering_guide: Young trees benefit from regular watering during dry spells; mature trees rely mainly on rainfall in the Philippines' humid rubber-growing regions (e.g.
guidance_source_title: Mindanao).
guidance_source_url: DA-Philippine Rubber Research Institute (PRRI) fertilization studies; Rubber Tree Production Guide
soil_moisture_sensor_note: "Young trees benefit from regular watering during dry spells; mature trees rely mainly on rainfall"
column10: Mature trees in humid regions (e.g. Mindanao) usually meet this range from rainfall alone.
